propositions: Every mutating Cloud transport member must be enumerated and classified by transport seam (ACLI subprocess, pooled direct REST, bare urlopen) and dispatch level (retrying wrapper, non-retrying apply phases, or no wrapper) to ensure 429 retry behavior is tested and documented at the correct boundary.

Cloud lacks a per-member 429 sweep covering all four distinct retry behaviors across transport and dispatch layers; mutations at different seams have opposite 429 handling (direct REST does not retry, subprocess backoff retries deliberately, dispatch wrapper retries deliberately) requiring layer-specific assertions rather than uniform one-attempt expectations.

Cloud has no config-validation tier equivalent to DC's hardened coverage; Cloud must assert non-HTTPS base URLs are rejected (or absence-document if not) and that missing credentials fail loudly rather than silently falling back to anonymous access.

Cloud's probe.py hardcodes RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES while DC reads runtime config; a Cloud deployment with non-standard workflow-defined resolved states cannot be probed correctly without a code change, warranting parity investigation of whether a runtime config hook is needed.

DC provides no user-search methods so _bootstrap_account_id_via_user_search degrades to string matching; this degradation is untested on the DC side, so an accidental rename on Cloud could produce silent breakage without detection.
